Blocks air flow more than it should - This is unlike the actual LG LT120F filter. The LG filter is a solid carbon block with holes allowing airflow. This product is a mesh with a fabric backing. Proper airflow is essential to the functioning of a refrigerator as air circulates from the freezer to the refrigerator and back to the freezer. The circulation fan is not powerful, and I am concerned that this 3rd-party filter will block the airflow. Air has to somehow make it through this fabric. The fabric is glued to the plastic and cannot easily be removed. LG refrigerators have enough problems already. The goal of this filter is to remove odors. Carbon does that. It is not designed to clean dust out of the air. So having a fabric filter is inappropriate for this product. Other third-party filters look like the LG one, where you can see through the holes to the other side.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This is a combination of a cap that has a pressure sensitive silicone release valve set into the middle of a solid bottom and a metal fine screen. You screw it onto the Aeropress instead of the usual cover.

COMES WITH EXTRA VALVE
This even came with an extra valve in it so you can replace it if you need to in the future. I hope it won't be necessary for a long time though.

HOW DOES IT PERFORM?
When I first used this, I was not sure what to expect. I was able to put the right amount of coffee into the tube, put the right amount of water, and the BAM- it stayed put!

Once I waited long enough, I pressed the plunger and it was amazing- the coffee came out nice and strong- in fact PERFECT. Even my fussy daughter liked it.

THE ONLY PROBLEM
The only problem if you want to call it that is that you won't get those perfect little pucks of pressed coffee grounds to pop into the compost. It still comes out, but not as compacted. No big deal, just thought you might want to know.

THE BOTTOM LINE
A PERFECT addition to my Aeropress, this little beauty makes great coffee even better. It keeps the grounds in the water just long enough to make a truly good cup of coffee. I love how it works, and even don't mind losing the satisfaction of popping little pucks of coffee into the compost.

MY RATING

For example, this icemaker cannot keep the ice frozen. So the ice cubes are made… Placed into a basket… And then you either remove them and use them or place them into your own freezer. Otherwise the ice simply melts and then will be refrozen.

The listing shows that this icemaker can make up to 33 pounds of ice per day. That is a bit of a misnomer, because the only way it can do that is if you constantly remove the ice day and night. So if this icemaker is in a location where there are people there around-the-clock, then yes it can make up to 33 pounds per day. As long as the ice is constantly being removed. But if you are at home, and using it simply for your family, then of course while you are sleeping you are not going to be removing the ice. One very nice thing that this particular model has that many others do not is the option to use a timer so that it will start and stop when you wanted to and not continue to make ice when you don’t need it to, like when you are sleeping.
